verdicts.evidence: lines 144-152 Save calls renameTeam; 158-171 Submit calls inviteMember and re-renders; 173-184 Remove calls removeMember and re-renders; 197 Refresh calls load. Every button has a handler that does what its label names.
line 48: hardcoded 'No members' row is shown before the load returns and for ever if it fails (139-141). line 128: new Date(null) renders a 1970 date for Sam Lee, who has no last-active value.
Single screen; no step depends on answers given on an earlier step or screen.
lines 39-40, 55-58: each task is one or two short inputs, one step, no free text longer than a line.
lines 145, 176: native confirm('Are you sure?') has OK as its default button, so Enter renames or removes the member. Invite role preselects member (line 58), which is safe.
Settings screen with six occasional tasks per the brief; no single dominant frequent task.
lines 27-30 hero, 32 intro paragraph, 33-35 three notes, 66 Refresh button: none match a task in the brief.
lines 41, 59, 66: one primary button in each card (Save, Submit, Refresh); row Remove buttons use the default secondary style (line 129).
line 129 Remove is secondary styled in the row, but line 176 confirm() makes OK the focused default, so Enter triggers the removal.
line 59: Submit starts disabled; lines 154-156 keep it disabled until the email matches a pattern. No text near it says why.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the file.
line 33: 'Note: this page was built with vanilla JavaScript and talks to a simulated API.'
lines 33-35: three callouts (Note, Tip, Disclaimer) at the top of the page, none tied to a decision or placed at an action.
line 32: 'This page lets you manage your team. Use the first card to rename the team, the table below it to...' narrates the interface.
lines 38-39: heading 'Team name' followed by label 'Team name'. lines 28-29: hero subtitle restates the heading, and line 32 says it again.
line 28: 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team'; line 29 'beautifully organised'; lines 148, 167 success toasts with exclamation marks.
line 59: invite button is labelled 'Submit'. line 41: 'Save' names no object. lines 145, 176: confirm dialogs offer the browser's OK and Cancel.

line 132: notification labels are the raw keys (weekly_digest, new_member). lines 58, 125-127: roles shown as lowercase enum values. lines 150, 169: e.message such as 'VALIDATION: email_format' shown to the user.

lines 150, 169, 182: raw server message shown ('ECONNRESET: socket hang up while trying to rename team', 'CONFLICT: member_exists') with no next step. line 189 'Failed to change role' gives no cause or next step.
line 169 'Error: ' prefix; line 182 'Failed: ' plus message; line 189 'Failed to change role'; server text in capitals (ECONNRESET, VALIDATION) passed through.
lines 121-130: with zero members the tbody is set to an empty string, leaving headers and nothing below. The static 'No members' at line 48 has no explanation or action.
lines 135-142: a failed load only logs to the console, leaving the static 'No members' row (line 48) with no retry message; a truly empty team shows a blank table. Causes are not told apart.
lines 139-141: load failure is console.error only. line 193: notification save failure is console.error only. line 161: the invite form is reset before the request, so a failure loses the email.
Calls take 0.4 to 1.5s (line 74). lines 135-138, 146-147, 164, 178, 188, 192: no loading or busy indicator is shown for any load or action.
line 48: 'No members' is in the initial markup and stays visible while getTeam is pending (lines 135-138); the team name field and notifications are blank meanwhile.

line 128: null lastActive becomes a 1970 date instead of a stated missing value. lines 19-20, 46: five-column table has no wrap, truncation or scroll container for the 56-character email; no media queries.
line 41: the team name is saved by an explicit Save. No beforeunload handler or persistence exists, and Refresh (lines 197, 120) overwrites an unsaved name edit without asking.

lines 55-56: the email field has only the label 'Email' and no format text, while lines 154-155 gate the button on a pattern. Whether the label alone states the rule is a judgement that came out differently on the second pass.
lines 39-40, 55-58: team name, invite email and invite role are all required; there are no optional fields.
lines 154-156: the input listener only toggles the button's disabled state; no error text is shown while typing. Errors appear only after submit (line 169).
lines 150, 169: rejections (email format, member exists, empty name) are shown in a browser alert, not beside the field, and the field is not marked.
line 161: $('invite-form').reset() runs before the request, so when inviteMember rejects (line 168-170) the email and role are gone.
lines 149-151, 168-170: on failure only an alert is shown; no focus move to the field, no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby anywhere in the file.
line 59: Submit is disabled on load; lines 154-156 enable it only once the email matches the pattern, with no indication of what is missing.
lines 144-152: Save is never disabled or given a busy state, so a second press sends renameTeam again. Invite is disabled during the request (line 162) but shows no busy state.
lines 146-147 rename, 178 remove, 188 role change, 192 notification: nothing visible changes between the click and the server answer up to 1.5s later.

line 193: a failed notification save is only logged, leaving the checkbox in the unsaved state. lines 139-141: a failed load or Refresh is not stated. line 188: a successful role change gives no sign it was saved.

line 167: 'Invite sent successfully!' toast appears while the new row is added to the table (165-166), but the sending of the invite itself is not otherwise visible. line 148 rename toast reports something not otherwise shown. Verdict differed on second pass.
line 116: every toast is removed after 2000ms, including the error toasts at lines 182 ('Failed: ...') and 189 ('Failed to change role').
line 145: renaming the team, which is reversible by renaming again, is gated by confirm('Are you sure?') and offers no undo.
line 176: removing a member (access lost at once) asks only 'Are you sure?' with the browser's OK and Cancel; it names neither the person nor the consequence, and OK is the default.
line 145: a confirmation dialog guards Save on the team name, a routine save.
lines 187-189: the role select shows the new value at once; on failure it is not put back, only a toast. lines 191-193: the checkbox stays in its new state on failure with no message.
lines 145, 176 confirm() and 150, 169 alert() are the only modals; each is a single decision or message and opens only after a user action.
lines 145, 150, 169, 176: only native browser confirm and alert dialogs are used; the browser handles focus, Escape and focus return, and they have a visible Cancel or OK.
lines 10-11, 27-30: a gradient hero with a 32px heading is the first and heaviest block; an intro paragraph and three notes (32-35) follow before the first working card at line 37.
lines 27-30: hero section with 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team' and a subtitle sits above the working content.
No summary numbers, stat cards or charts in the markup (lines 26-68).
No filter, search or sort controls exist for the members table (lines 44-50).
lines 40-41, 56-59, 66, 124-129, 132: all controls are native inputs, selects, checkboxes and buttons, and dialogs are native confirm and alert; nothing is click-only on a non-focusable element.
lines 8-22: colour is not used to show status, errors, required fields or selection; roles and messages are text.
lines 112-117: toasts are a div appended to body with no role or aria-live; no live region exists in the page markup (lines 26-68).
Only native select elements are used (lines 58, 124); there are no accordions, custom menus, disclosure buttons or tabs.

lines 8-22: no media queries; the five-column members table (46-48) has no reflow or scroll wrapper, so at 375px with the long email the Remove column is pushed off the viewport. The brief says phones are used.
